cases.title: A new pipe joins the only pit at its end
cases.expected: CD draws a pipe from the new pit P8; the command line says 'Inserted flow arrow. Flow: P8 -> Open end' and 'End is free: open end flagged, connect it later.' once (the far end is free by design); the pipe's first vertex lies inside the pit's catch reach; the line never says the flow starts from an open end (the BUG-560 drift).
cases.why_not_unit: The join is made by the live CD point landing against the real pit in the drawing.
not_automated: Pit Schedule row P8 shows outlet IL 18.000 and the pipe's diameter (D03 assertion 3): the runner cannot read the Pit Schedule rows yet. Not part of this case.
The pit outline is not read. The catch reach is approximated as a circle of 641 mm around the pit insertion point (half the 600 x 900 default pit diagonal 541 mm plus the 100 mm catch).

cases.title: PIT and CD keep placing until Esc, and Esc keeps what was placed
cases.expected: After PIT and CD each places one object and offers the next, the command line says so; each Esc ends it with the 'Stopped' line and keeps what was placed (one new pit at 150000,-80000, at least one new pipe polyline, texts and arrow); no second New Pit or New Pipe window opens after an Esc; ONE U takes away the new pipe, its IL texts and its arrow and leaves the pit; the Civil log holds one outcome line for PIT and one for CD (the word is recorded, not judged: BUG-862).
cases.why_not_unit: The run is a chain of real AutoCAD command instances queued one behind another. Only live AutoCAD shows the next prompt, the Esc ending and what U takes back.
not_automated: Exactly one new pipe object: the composition of the new objects (how many polylines, blocks, texts) has never been read, so it is recorded here and only 'at least one' is asserted.
The 'Command outcome' words for PIT and CD are recorded, not judged (BUG-862: Esc-ended placements log 'cancelled').

cases.title: CE never saves the drawing: the file stays unchanged until the drafter saves
cases.expected: After placing a pit and a pipe and running CDSYNC, CDRECOVERINVERTS and opening and closing PITSCHEDULE, the drawing file on disk has the same SHA-256 and last-written time as when AutoCAD opened it, and the only new files beside it are CE's own _PRE_C7_ backups.
cases.why_not_unit: Only the real file on disk after a real AutoCAD session shows whether anything wrote to it.
not_automated: This case runs AFTER R01 has undone its pipe (U must be the last undoable command in R01), so CDSYNC and CDRECOVERINVERTS work on the fixture drawing itself; the checks only prove they ran and that the file on disk did not change.
CDREBUILD wording 'it does not save the drawing itself' (D18 assertion 2): CDREBUILD was dropped from this case because it has never been driven and its prompts are unknown.
